claims.text: The starting material is a homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy.
The starting Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy has a dual-phase lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
The FCC/B2 interfaces in the starting alloy are incoherent.
Stress concentration at the incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces makes the starting alloy brittle.
Applying 6 GPa at 1473 K for 2 hours will cause a topological transformation of the lamellar microstructure.
The HPHT-induced transformation will produce a hierarchically patterned microstructure.
The HPHT treatment will convert incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces into coherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces will facilitate dislocation transfer between the two phases.
Dislocation transfer across coherent interfaces will reduce interfacial stress concentration.
The treated alloy will activate dislocation slip, stacking faults, and twinning during deformation.
The coherent hierarchical microstructure will promote homogeneous strain distribution.
Homogeneous strain distribution will arrest cracking at FCC/B2 interfaces.
At high strain, the GND densities in the FCC and B2 phases of the treated sample will converge.
The treated sample will exhibit elongated crack morphology rather than isolated microcracks.
The HPHT treatment will significantly improve ductility without sacrificing strength.
Approximately 6 GPa and 1473 K fall within a processing window that induces the desired transformation without melting or unwanted phase decomposition.
Conventional thermal-mechanical treatments fail to produce the same hierarchical interface coherence or GND homogenization.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says interfacial cracking is arrested, whereas elongated crack propagation is designated as the favorable treated morphology and isolated microcracks as falsifying. Without explaining that the elongated cracks are non-interfacial or otherwise less damaging, elongated propagation is in tension with crack arrest.
